To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose and implement a scalable layer- agnostic packet classification framework that eliminates per-packet state in classifiers and incentivizes collaborators to help with classification.

We propose Lattice, a scalable layer-agonstic packet classification framework that generalizes classifier designs and enables offloading computation and memory requirements of packet classifiers to collaborators (e..g, end hosts).

we propose a scalable layer agnostic packet classification framework that enables offloading part computation and memory requirements of classifiers to collaborators (e. g. endhosts) and is incentive compatible in the sense that collaborators cannot get a better service by lying.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a scalable, incentive compatible, and semantically equivalent layer-agnostic framework for high speed packet classification.
the design of scalable and incentive compatible layer-agnostic packet classifiers.
the design of a framework that allows packet classification at different layers to scale well with the number of classification rules and the rate of incoming packets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Lattice enables scalable and efficient layer-agnostic packet classifiers.
Lattice enables a scalable and efficient packet classification framework.
Lattice is a scalable layer-agnositic packet classification framework that generalizes classifier desgin and enables offloading of computation and memory requirement to collaborators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Lattice enables scalable and efficient packet classification by offloading part of the computation to collaborators.

Lattice enables scalable and efficient packet classification by eliminating per-packet classification, offloading part of the classification process to collaborators, and incentivizing deployment by giving preferentially treatment to collaborators.
we present a framework that enables offloading packet classification to end hosts, which in turn enables high speed packet classification with a large number of rules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current state-of-the-art in packet classification is far from ideal
packet classification can be made more scalable by offloading part of the computation to end hosts.
Lattice enables scalable packet classification by offloading part of the computation and memory requirements of packet classifiers to collaborators.
